Population Growth
What this shows
How many people live in each 1km cell of Lahore district, from measured counts (2015-2030) through five diverging scenario projections to 2050.
Data sources
HDX Pakistan provides observed population counts at 1km resolution from 2015 to 2030. At the 2025 crossover point, the data transitions to WorldPop FuturePop SSP projections. The scenario toggle is greyed out before 2025 because before that year, there is only one past — the measured one. SSP2 and SSP4 are synthesized as per-cell means of their bracketing scenarios and this is disclosed here.
What to look for
The log color scale makes the spatial story visible. The historical core through Gulberg is already saturated near 20,000 people per km². New scenario growth does not deepen the red in the center — it spreads orange into peri-urban cells to the south and east.
Key finding
At 2050, SSP1 and SSP5 diverge by over 600,000 people — roughly a Faisalabad-sized city appearing or not appearing depending on the development pathway. Toggle between them at 2050 and watch the outer ring shift.
At 2050, a Faisalabad-sized city appears or disappears depending on the scenario chosen.
SSP Scenarios
1 Sustainable — green growth, cooperation
2 Middle road — current trends continue
3 Rivalry — fragmented, high emissions
4 Inequality — elites adapt, rest don't
5 Fossil growth — fastest warming
